Replay

Waves and held channels

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Director to pace waves with bounded spawn work, and Channel for sustained interactions whose duration belongs in the simulation. Wave describes a count and a post-clear rest in ticks. Director owns the current wave, pending spawns, live count, rest deadline and completion flag. Put it in the world when it determines gameplay; it then travels with rollback and checkpoints.

director_tick announces a new wave, starts spawning on the following tick, and admits at most one spawn per call. Pass can_spawn=false when there is no storage or valid prey: pending/live counts stay unchanged. Report directed deaths through director_note_death. Its overflow failure preserves the prior director state. The game decides what and where to spawn and which bodies belong to the director.

Odin
next := world.director
count, started := p.director_tick(&next, ctx.tick, waves, has_room)
if count > 0 && !spawn_enemy(world, ctx) {return}
world.director = next

Channel is a tick-owned sustained hold. channel_tick restarts when its target identity changes, clears on target zero, and returns true once at completion. The game must validate continuing range, liveness and input eligibility every tick. Use a lifetime-qualified target key. The simulation advances the duration, so the authority can enforce it rather than accepting owner-streamed progress.

Fifty 400-tick director traces match the original procedures compiled in isolation. Native tests cover storage backpressure, rest/completion and interrupted/retargeted channels; the helpers also type-check for freestanding WASM.
